title: Films where a protagonist murders, feels guilty about it, but then is never punished.

commenti.body:
Can't see the other comments, but >!Match Point!< is one that came into my head. >!It's interesting to compare this with the directors life: Allen has been accused of some monstrous things. Even if you don't believe he is a child molester, he had an affair with his stepdaughter (who you can see as an extra in Hannah and Her Sisters when she was 12) and later married her. They're still married, but it's interesting that someone like him would make a movie about doing something horrible and then having a happy ever after.!<

Oh, and arguably, >!The Talented Mr Riply and the similar movie, Saltburn.!< Depending on 1. where you stop or 2. how much you believe in the protagonist's remorse.

**Investigation of a citizen under suspicion (1970)** is perfect for you

others could be: 

-	in the bedroom (2001) kind of does that, but the guilt is not the central part of the film. 

-	the vanishing (1988) deals with the getting away part but not the guilt.
